analysis.title: FX Risk Index: Risk sentiment continues to moderate
key_insights: The CACIB FX Risk Index is at -0.7779 versus -0.9385 last week, reflecting a further reduction in risk-seeking activity by investors.

The Risk Index is above its 100-day moving average for the first time since April, before the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding was signed. Moves of the Index above its trend have historically led to a sustained reduction in risk-seeking behaviour.

Investor risk appetite keeps waning as key geopolitical events approach. The Israeli election is too close to call. A change of government would probably alter Israel's diplomatic tone more than its security doctrine.

Netanyahu favours regime change in Iran, while Gadi Eisenkot has not explicitly called for the regime's downfall. A more moderate PM could make it tougher for Trump to ramp back up military action against Iran, a key risk after the US midterms next Tuesday.
The AI trade has partly revived. Anthropic's official IPO filing and Meta's USD25bn share sale, five times oversubscribed, helped sentiment. Oracle deepened its partnership with OpenAI.
Microsoft and Meta report earnings later today and Amazon and Intel report Thursday. The report expects these to have a significant impact on sentiment.

The FOMC decision later today is expected to be an on-hold. The statement rhetoric and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference are the largest influences on rates and sentiment. A dovish hold would be positive for risk.

Other than lower gold prices, all factors contributed to the rise in the Risk Index over the past week. Higher equity volatility and defensive stocks outperforming cyclicals were the largest contributors.
Among G10 currencies, only CHF, CAD and SEK have significant positive correlations with the Risk Index. GBP, USD and NOK have significant negative correlations.
earnings_insights: Microsoft and Meta report earnings on 28 October 2026 (later today per the report). Amazon and Intel report Thursday. No estimates are given.
